message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling *detailed* interface information on the most common platforms. If you’re working with a particular vendor or operating system, let me know and I can drill down further. | Platform | Typical command(s) | What you’ll see | Tips | |----------|-------------------|-----------------|------| | **Cisco IOS / IOS XE** | `show interface `
`show interface detail`
`show interface status`
`show ip interface brief` | • MAC address
• MTU, duplex, speed
• Admin/oper status
• Errors, collisions, CRCs
• IP address (if configured)
• Interface description | Use `include`/`exclude` to filter output. For all interfaces: `show interface status`. For SNMP, OID `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1` (ifIndex). | | **Cisco NX‑OS** | `show interface `
`show interface detail`
`show interface status` | Same as IOS, plus additional NX‑OS fields (e.g., `link-local` IP, `port-channel` membership). | Use `show interface counters` for per‑interface stats. | | **Juniper Junos** | `show interfaces `
`show interfaces detail`
`show interfaces terse` | • MAC, MTU, speed, duplex
• Admin/oper status
• Errors, discards, CRCs
• IP address (if configured)
• Description | `show interfaces statistics` for counters. SNMP OID `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1` (ifIndex). | | **Arista EOS** | `show interface `
`show interface detail` | Similar to Junos; includes `link-local` IP, `port-channel` info. | `show interface counters` for stats. | | **Linux (CLI)** | `ip link show `
`ethtool `
`cat /sys/class/net//address` | • MAC address
• MTU, speed, duplex
• Admin/oper status
• Link detected
• Driver info | `ethtool -S ` for driver counters. | | **Windows (CLI)** | `netsh interface ipv4 show interface `
`Get-NetAdapter -Name ""` | • MAC address
• Speed, duplex
• Status
• Driver info | PowerShell cmdlets give richer data (`Get-NetAdapterStatistics`). | | **SNMP** | OIDs:
`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1` (ifIndex)
`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2` (ifDescr)
`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8` (ifOperStatus)
`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.9` (ifInOctets) | Pull any field via SNMP walk/GET. | Use community string `public` for read‑only. | | **REST API (e.g., Arista CloudVision, Cisco DNA Center)** | `GET /api/v1/interfaces/` | JSON payload with all interface attributes. | Requires authentication token. | --- ### How to decide which method to use 1. **CLI vs. API** – If you have console access, CLI is fastest. If you’re automating or integrating, use SNMP or REST. 2. **All interfaces vs. one** – `show interface status` (Cisco) or `show interfaces terse` (Juniper) gives a quick table. For deep dive, use the `detail` variant. 3. **Counters** – Look for `counters`, `statistics`, or `-S` (Linux ethtool) to get traffic/error counts. 4. **Configuration vs. Operational** – `show running-config interface ` (Cisco) shows config; `show interface ` shows operational state. --- #### Example: Cisco IOS ```bash # Quick table of all interfaces show interface status # Detailed view of GigabitEthernet0/1 show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail # Show only errors show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 counters | include error # SNMP walk for all interface descriptions snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2 ``` #### Example: Linux ```bash # Basic info ip link show eth0 # Driver counters ethtool -S eth0 # Full sysfs view cat /sys/class/net/eth0/operstate cat /sys/class/net/eth0/mtu ``` --- ### Next Steps - **Specify your platform** if you need a step‑by‑step walkthrough. - **Automation** – If you’re scripting, consider using libraries like `netmiko` (Python) for SSH or `pysnmp` for SNMP. - **Troubleshooting** – Look at error counters (`input errors`, `output errors`) and link status to diagnose problems. Let me know which environment you’re targeting, and I can provide a tailored command set or script!
